facts.topic: MobEquipment identifies the known local player through network identity and subclient
facts.contract: The recovered player branch obtains UserEntityIdentifierComponent and compares its NetworkIdentifier against ClientNetworkSystem::tryGetLocalNetworkId, including identifier type/type-data equality and the sender subclient ID. This distinguishes the local-player branch from the remote-player inventory/equipment branch.

facts.topic: Known-local MobEquipment selects the hotbar and does not replace the item
facts.contract: For the known local player, container0 calls PlayerInventory::selectSlot with mSelectedSlot. It does not replace the hotbar stack from the packet item or slot fields. Every nonzero container, including offhand119, leaves this local inventory/selection branch without mutation. Remote equipment has a separate offhand119 branch and must not be substituted for the known-local behavior.

facts.topic: selectSlot ignores invalid indices and stores the supplied container
facts.contract: PlayerInventory::selectSlot returns before mutation when its unsigned selected slot is greater than8, including negative signed values reinterpreted as unsigned. Valid0..8 stores mSelected and mSelectedContainerId. A nonzero supplied container or an unchanged slot skips the later Inventory0 change side effects. The recovered client-side level branch skips the server-side selection event path.

facts.topic: PlayerHotbar forwards its container and separately refreshes the top scene
facts.contract: With a local player and mShouldSelectSlot=true, PlayerHotbar forwards mSelectedSlot and mContainerId unchanged to selectSlot. Unlike the local MobEquipment branch, it does not require container0 first. Independently of shouldSelectSlot, it calls onInternetUpdate on a nonnull top scene, then marks the packet handled. The implementation of every selected-container consumer and UI refresh is outside this narrow dispatch contract.
